chunks.title: SMOM 26-003: Processing 09M/CAT-IV FY26
chunks.text:
NATIONAL GUARD BUREAU
  111 SOUTH GEORGE MASON DRIVE
  ARLINGTON VA 22204-1373

ARNG-HRR (RN 600A)  1 October 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention (RRF)

SUBJECT: SMOM 26-003 - Processing 09M and CAT IV-A Applicants for Enlistment
in FY26

1. References.

  a. AR 601-210 (Regular Army and Reserve Components Enlistment Program)

  b. ARNG Personnel Policy Division, ARNG-HRH memorandum (FY26 Army National
Guard Accession Options Criteria, PPOM 25-042), 30 September 2025

 c. Department of Defense Instruction 1145.01, “Qualitative Distribution of Military
Manpower,” 12 December 2013, incorporating Change 2, 4 May 2020

2. Purpose: This SMOM provides the processing procedures and CAT IV-A allocations
for FY26. All 09M (T7) enlistments will be the primary vehicle for recruiting CAT IVs.
States, Territories and Districts are allocated a certain number of allowable CAT IV-A
because ARNG must adhere to the 4% CAT IV requirement outlined in the Qualitative
Distribution of Military Manpower Policy. Throughout the year, the CAT IV-A percentage
will encompass 09M enlistments, 16-20/Tier 2 CAT IV-A’s, and FLRI (09C) enlistments.

   a. Program Utilization. The ARNG offers three enlistment options for CAT IV-A
applicants based on aptitude and qualifications outlined in paragraph 1(c) of this
document. RRBs are charged with the responsibility to appropriately use, manage, and
track all CAT IV-A accessions.

  (1) Traditional CAT IV-A (AFQT 16-20)

  (2) Future Soldier Preparatory Course/09M CAT IV-A (AFQT 21-30)

  (3) Foreign Language Recruiting Initiative (FLRI)/09C CAT IV-A (AFQT 21-30)

3. Traditional CAT IV-A Enlistments.

  a. CAT IV-A packets are required to be completed and ready for enlistment when
added to the Order of Merit List (OML) CAT IV Tracker-OML

ARNG-HRR-O
SUBJECT: Processing 09M and CAT IV-A Applicants for Enlistment in FY26

  (1) States will not project applicants for enlistment until they are in an
“Approved” status in the Special Programs Tracker, located in MS Teams.

  (2) Traditional CAT IVs were allocated by States, Territories and Districts
based on the FY26 mission letter. States should exhaust all allocations within the
assigned quarter (see enclosure). The ROC will not authorize allocations to be rolled
over to the following quarter.

  (3) CAT IVs will be restricted in the 4th quarter to ensure the overall CAT IV
percentage is under the threshold and we can fill FY26 09M seats.

 b. Enlistment Criteria:

  (1) 16-20 AFQT or 16-30 AFQT (Tier II education).

  (2) Must have at least two valid ASVAB scores.

  (3) Current Physical and DAT results required (approved medical waiver
if applicable).

  (4) Meet initial entry body fat standards (ARMS and ARMS Expanded are not
authorized to enlist as a Traditional CAT IV).

  (5) Meet MOS line score requirements, eligible for Line Score Waiver,
or received a proponent exception.

  (6) No ARNG-HRR/DARNG level conduct waivers (IAW AOC).

  (7) Select a primary vacancy/MOS that ships within 90 days. Reference
  General | NGB-ARNG-HRR-MEPS | Microsoft Teams

  (8) Encouraged to attend at least one RSP drill.

  (9) Enlist for a 3x5 or 6x2 year contract.

  c. Traditional CAT IV-A’s Approved on the OML will be open for enlistment 1
January 2026. Enclosed are the state-by-state allocations for Traditional CAT IV
enlistments authorized for FY26. At the end of each quarter, NGB will reevaluate the
CAT IV-A percentage and may authorize additional enlistments if justified.

  2

ARNG-HRR-O
SUBJECT: Processing 09M and CAT IV-A Applicants for Enlistment in FY26

  d. 09M Open Enlistment.

  (1) 09Ms (T7) will be open for enlistment 1 Oct 2025 until all current FY26
training seats are exhausted (excludes High School Seniors). Once all seats are filled,
further guidance will be provided by the ROB.

  (2) High School Seniors (HSSR) will be eligible for enlistment into the 09M (T7)
program on 1 January 2026.

  (3) Required to take first available training.

  (4) For eligibility requirements, please refer to the AOC Appendix K.

4. CAT IV/09M accessions may be closed at any time without prior notice. The ROC
will continuously assess CAT IV accessions to determine DoD ARNG CAT IV
percentage compliance.

5. This memorandum remains valid until 30 September 2026.

6. Requests for exception to policy (HRR 111) will be processed through NGB
ROC via MS Teams ETP_HRR_Form_111.

7. POC for this action is MSG Janelle Taua-Freitas at janelle.a.taua-freitas.mil@army.mil
or 571-644-2801.

chunks.title: SMOM 25-028: Suitability Screening Requirements
chunks.text:
NATIONAL GUARD BUREAU
  111 SOUTH GEORGE MASON DRIVE
  ARLINGTON VA 22204-1382

ARNG-HRR (600-37a)  22 September 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard (ARNG) Recruiting and Retention Force

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

1. References. See Appendix A.

2. Background. Army Regulation 600-78, Army Suitability, Fitness, and Credentialing
Program (8 March 2024) takes precedence over all other departmental issuances affecting the
suitability, fitness and credentialing program. The updated regulation establishes suitability,
fitness, and credentialing policies for military positions of trust and other positions screened for
suitability.

3. Purpose. This policy provides clarifying guidance to the ARNG Recruiting and Retention
Force (RRF) to support compliance with the Army Personnel Suitability Screening Program for
applicable duty positions. This program supports and provides a measure of assurance that
individuals serving in positions screened for suitability are of good character, reputation and
trustworthiness which promotes the efficiency and integrity of the recruiting program. This
memorandum supersedes SMOM 25-005.

4. Applicability. This policy applies to ARNG AGR, ADOS, FTNGD-OS and M-day personnel
regardless of rank performing a direct recruiting function that supports the accomplishment of
the recruiting mission. Direct recruiting functions for the purpose of this policy are defined as all
actions related to the prospecting, processing, and accessioning processes for ARNG
enlistments to include all officer and warrant officer producing programs. These are functions
requiring frequent and direct unrestricted contact with applicants, prospects, trainees and
warriors. Direct recruiting functions also include all actions from assignment to the Recruit
Sustainment Program (RSP) and from initial contact to shipping the Warrior to Initial Active-Duty
Training (IADT). Included categories are further defined below.

   a. Recruiting Cadre.

  (1) This includes all Soldiers performing production Recruiting and Retention NCO
(RRNCO) duties with a 4 or 5-digit Recruiting Station Identification (RSID). It also includes
Recruiting and Retention Section Chiefs (RRSC), Region NCOICs, or Company First Sergeants
with a 3-digit RSID, Military Entrance Processing Station Guidance Counselors, Soldiers holding
the primary military occupational specialty (MOS) of 79T, special qualification identifier code 4
(SQI-4) and supporting personnel.

  (2) Supporting personnel include all Soldiers performing support functions requiring
frequent and direct contact with applicant, prospect, trainees and warriors. This also includes all
79T personnel entering the T10 AGR program.

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

   b. Training Cadre. All Recruit Sustainment Program (RSP) Cadre and Drill Sergeants,
regardless of the MOS or duty status, who work with RSP Soldiers during Inactive Duty Training
weekend for RSP or Direct Ship training. This includes Enlisted Reserve and Officer Training
Corps (ROTC) Cadre (ARNG).

   c. Officers/Warrant Officers. ROTC Cadre including Assistant Professors of Military Science
(APMS) and Professors of Military Science (PMS), Officer Strength Managers, Warrant Officer
Strength Managers, and Officers at the Company/Region level and below.

   d. Command Teams. All Battalion, Company, and Region Command Teams (Commander
and Senior Enlisted Advisors) including MOS immaterial Recruiting Battalion Command
Sergeants Major require suitability screening.

   e. Excepted Personnel. Recruiting battalion staff who do not perform recruiting duties,
recruiting command headquarters staff, recruiting and retention NCOs serving on battalion staff
who do not perform a direct recruiting function are exempt from the screening requirements,
unless nominated for another position screened for suitability.

5. Screening Process. All screening requirements must be met prior to assignment or upon
reassignment to another position screened for suitability. This includes incorporating
screenings into the hiring selection processes. The screening process consists of two parts,
local and centralized screening requirements. Commanders will complete all local screening
requirements prior to submission for centralized screening.

   a. Local Screening. Soldiers must disclose any pending or prior offense that may prevent
their approval for appointment to a suitability position by completing HRR Form 600 (Enclosure
1, Suitability Questionnaire).

  (1) The Recruiting and Retention Battalion (RRB) Recruiting and Training Cadre
Suitability representative will ensure a medical record review is conducted. This includes
verification of a current Periodic Health Assessment (PHA) and a review of any MOS-specific
PULHES requirements.

  (2) Commanders will verify with local security managers that all personnel nominated to
designated positions have a favorable National Agency Check with Local Agency Check and
Credit (NACLC), Tier 3 Investigation or higher background investigation.

  (3) The RRB Recruiting and Training Cadre Suitability representative will conduct a
search for the Soldier’s name on the National Sex Offender Public Website
(http://www.nsopw.gov). The Recruiting and Retention Commander (RRC) will print and sign a
copy of the search results.

  (4) The RRB will conduct local law enforcement screening utilizing DD Form 369 (Police
Record Check) to verify state/local criminal screenings.

  (5) If derogatory information is identified during a local screening, the RRB must indicate
the derogatory information in the screening memo (Enclosure 2, Memorandum Examples).

  2

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

Supporting information and/or documentation regarding the derogatory information may be
included with screening request.

   b. Centralized Screening. The centralized screening process begins once the local
screening is complete, and the screening request (Enclosure 3, Suitability Screening Request)
has been submitted to Recruiting Standards Branch (RSB) via encrypted email (ng.ncr.ngb-
arng.mbx.hrr-suitability@army.mil) or through DoD Safe (https://safe.apps.mil). Recruiting
commands are responsible for ensuring screening packets are complete, accurate and
submitted NLT than 120 days prior to expiration of screening date or if a military course
prerequisite. This ensures results are received prior to appointment, avoiding lapses in
rescreening or military course prerequisites. Failure to adhere to the above standards can
result in processing delays or a return without action/for correction.

  (1) All screening requests submissions must contain complete and accurate data for the
required fields provided on the RSB Suitability Screening Request. This is in addition to the
memorandum verifying completion of local screening requirements signed by the RRC
(Enclosure 2, Memorandum Examples). Multiple names may be included on a single
memorandum submission. No further delegation is authorized for RRC signature requirements.

  (2) The RSB will review the documents for accuracy and completeness. The centralized
screening process will not begin for any Soldier that does not have a signed screening
memorandum validating local screening requirements have been complete.

  (3) Centralized screening includes review by the Department of Army Inspector General
(DAIG), Criminal Investigation Command, the Soldier’s Official Military Personnel File (OMPF),
and the Army Substances Abuse Program (ASAP). These four national level screening results
check for disqualifying offenses as outlined in AR 600-78. (See Appendix B for a listing of
disqualifying offenses by Type.)

  (4) Upon completion of the above-mentioned checks, Special Actions Personnel Division,
(ARNG-HRP-R), will initially identify all personnel as cleared or as having a Type I, Type II,
Type III, or administrative disqualification. The RSB will verify all HRP-R results and will notify
the RRC of the findings through a derogatory information notification memorandum. If further
clarification is required for offense determination, a request for additional information will be sent
to the RRB point of contact.

  (5) The RRC will complete the HRR Form 600-1 (Enclosure 4, Suitability Screening
Checklist) at the end of the screening process for each Soldier performing recruiting and training
cadre duties and annotate centralized screening date. These forms will be maintained by the
RRB Suitability manager IAW Army Records Information Management System (ARIMS)
requirements.

   c. Suitability Rescreening. Rescreening requests are required every three years prior to the
expiration of the Soldier’s current screening, if they remain assigned to a qualifying position or
duty. The process and screening requirement remain the same as outlined above. RSB will
publish monthly notifications to RRBs for expired/pending expiration of personnel to assist in
meeting this requirement. Disqualifying information uncovered during a rescreen requires

  3

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

suspension or removal from designated position unless an appeal or rebuttal was previously
approved for the offense.

  d. Soldiers who have new derogatory information discovered or reported during a rescreen
follow the same process and procedures as outlined further in this policy for suspension,
removal, appeal submission and rebuttal. New derogatory information, based upon type and
circumstances, may additionally meet the reporting requirements for recruiter irregularity and/or
misconduct.

  e. Conduct will be considered regardless of issues resulting in formal charges or
administrative or legal action. Conduct that may have resulted in dismissal, expungement or a
finding of not guilty by a court or other entities in the civilian or military justice system may still
be considered for suitability and fitness adjudications using the preponderance of the evidence
standard but will be adjudicated as a Type II or Type III offense.

6. Suspension and Removal. Soldiers that have been disqualified from Suitability positions
due to derogatory information discovered during Suitability screenings or while assigned to a
position requiring suitability are suspended until an adjudication of an approved appeal (if
authorized) or rebuttal. Suspension from recruiting duty is the temporary removal of a
Recruiting and Training Cadre member from all contact with prospects and applicants for
enlistment and from the processing of any documentation concerning active applications for
enlistments to include officer-producing programs, or RSP duties involving direct contact with
RSP Warriors.

   a. For Soldiers serving in positions screened for Suitability the removal authority (1st O6 in
the chain of command) must immediately suspend and temporarily reassign a Soldier upon
notification that the Soldier is under investigation for an offense, or upon notification there is
adverse information that the Soldier has committed a disqualifying offense. See Enclosure 2 for
example template for the O6 suspension format. A copy of the suspension will be provided to
RSB upon completion of the notification.

  (1) The Recruiter Systems Network (RSN) Account Suspension. The RSB may initiate
the suspension process of RSN account access for noncompliant personnel.

  (2) The RSB will send notification of noncompliance to the RRC 30 days prior to the
suspension of a Soldier’s RSN account. If the Soldier becomes suitability compliant prior to
RSN account suspension, the account will not be suspended. Once the RSB has confirmed
initiation of the required screening request or an approved appeal, the RSN account will be
reactivated.

  b. The command must flag Soldiers under investigation in accordance with references listed
in Appendix A and monitor the investigation until complete. In the event a Soldier is
permanently removed from Suitability screened positions the correct Assignment Eligibility and
Availability (AEA) restriction code will be added using current personnel management guidance
and listed references.

  4

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

   c. If the investigation result is unsubstantiated, the command must notify the removal
authority to lift the suspension. In the event of disqualifying information that is later proven to be
inaccurate or does not meet the standard for disqualification, RSB will publish an administrative
correction memorandum to allow the Soldier to continue suitability screened duties.

   d. If the investigation is substantiated or if the command receives adverse information of an
offense, the command must provide the disqualifying information to the removal authority.
Soldiers who have been removed from a position screened for suitability for a Type I are
ineligible for future appointments to other positions screened for suitability.

7. Appeal Process.

  a. Based on the type of disqualifying offense; Soldiers have a right to submit an appeal for
adjudication. Appeal requests are submitted by the Soldier through the chain of command to
the approval authority. Non-endorsement or recommendations of disapproval by the Soldier’s
chain of command does not prevent the packet from moving forward to the appeal approval
authority. Once an appeal is adjudicated favorably for a specific offense, there is no
requirement for resubmission of an appeal on future re-screenings if the same offense
information is found on a rescreening.

  (1) Type I offenses are permanently disqualifying and may not be appealed. Type I
offenses that do not result in a criminal conviction or finding of guilty in a field grade Article 15
UCMJ proceeding will be treated as Type II offenses.

  (2) Type II offenses may be appealed through the Soldier’s chain of command through
RSB to the appellate authority for decision.

  (3) Type III offenses may be approved/adjudicated by the 1st General Officer in the chain
of command and appealed at the State Adjutant General level.

  (4) Administrative reports are only disqualifying for an initial appointment. Once the
administrative report is resolved favorably, the individual will be cleared for suitability
requirements.

   b. Timeline. Soldiers have 14 days from notification to submit a memorandum requesting
reconsideration for approval or appeal or notifying their intent to rebut incorrect information .
Commanders may grant an extension up to 30 days in writing to be included with the request.
Soldiers will have 45 days from notification to submit documents in defense, extenuation or
mitigation. Commanders may grant extensions for extenuating circumstances beyond the
Soldier’s control. These documents are also submitted through the chain of command to the
approval or appeal authority.

   c. Appeal packets at a minimum will consist of the following items (Enclosure 5, Appeals
Checklist). Additionally, information and further recommendations regarding memorandum
submissions can be found in Enclosure 2.

  5

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

  (1) Soldier’s memorandum outlining the circumstances of the offense, mitigating factors
or other extenuating circumstances and requesting appeal or adjudication

  (2) Battalion Commander’s endorsement memorandum for the adjudication or appeal
and if applicable, extension memorandums.

  (3) First Colonel (O6) in the chain of command’s endorsement memorandum and O6
Suspension memorandum (if not previously submitted to RSB).

  (4) State Adjutant General (TAG) endorsement memorandum.

  (5) State Judge Advocate General (SJA) legal review on offense (disqualifying
information is credible and supported by a preponderance of the evidence).

  (6) Offense documents and any legal records showing final disposition of all charges or
other supporting documents as appropriate.

   d. Appeal packets missing any of these documents will be returned without action to the
RRB for correction. Soldiers that choose not to request an appeal must decline in writing
through their chain of command with a copy provided to the RSB. Upon receipt of the
declination of appeal, RRBs will impose the correct assignment eligibility restriction codes to the
disqualified Soldier’s file.

   e. Approvals and appeals should only be granted in extenuating circumstances, when the
approval or appeal authority determines that, despite the disqualifying information, the Soldier
requesting the adjudication or submitting the appeal is best qualified to serve in the position.
Approvals and appeals should not be granted if the disqualifying information calls into question
the character, conduct, or personal integrity of the Soldier requesting the adjudication.

8. Rebuttals. Soldiers have the right to submit a rebuttal if they believe the disqualifying
information is erroneous. All Type II rebuttals will be submitted and routed through the Soldier’s
chain of command to the RSB for processing to the approval authority. The rebuttal checklist
will be used for submissions (Enclosure 5). Rebuttal approval authorities are the same as
appeal approval authorities (based on offense type).

  a. Soldiers intending to rebut must notify the appointing or removal authority within 14
calendar days from receipt of the disqualification notification. Rebuttals must be submitted in a
memorandum stating intent to submit matters refuting the accuracy of the disqualifying
information. Commanders may grant an extension of up to 30 total days or through the next
scheduled drilling period. Extension memorandums must accompany the requested rebuttal.

  b. Soldiers have forty-five (45) calendar days to submit supporting documentation refuting
the accuracy of the disqualification. Soldier rebuttals must be accompanied by the chain of
command’s recommendations (endorsement or non-endorsement of the request) to the
approval authority as outlined in Enclosure 6, Rebuttal checklist.

  6

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

  c. Rebuttal requests and endorsements should factually support why the disqualifying
offense information is believed to be erroneous.

9. Responsibilities.

   a. Recruiting and Retention Commander will:

  (1) Appoint and maintain a Recruiting and Training Cadre Suitability representative(s)
(Enclosure 9, Suitability Reporting Compliance Verification), to collect local level screening
results for Soldiers nominated to serve in, or currently serving in recruiting and training cadre
positions. These appointed personnel will maintain the Suitability Tracker provided by the RSB
and will serve as the point of contact for the Battalion.

  (2) Provide required information pertaining to ARNG Recruiting and Training Cadre
Suitability screening reporting. (See Enclosure 8 for the Quarterly Reporting Template.) Ensure
their RRB submits the quarterly report to the RSB 15 business days before the end of each
quarter (Example: 1st QTR: 15 December; 2nd QTR: 15 March; 3rd QTR: 15 Jun; 4th QTR: 15
September). The RSB Form 2A will be submitted biannually with the December and June
HQDA G1 reporting periods.

  (3) Ensure their Suitability representative notifies RSB of any out processing or removed
Suitability screened personnel within (30) calendar days of the removal (e.g. Transfer, PCS,
Retirement etc.). Updates will be submitted with the following information: Rank, Last Name,
First Name, DoDID, State, and removal reason (ETS, Transfer, Retire, etc.) to the RSB
Suitability Group email. Upon verification, RSB will move those individuals from the States
Active folder to Inactive folder in the Suitability Compliance Tracker to ensure accuracy of
reporting data. Suitability representatives will conduct tracker reviews for their RRB’s population
quarterly, at a minimum, in support of HQDA G1 quarterly reporting requirements.

  (4) Ensure suspended or removed personnel are not performing direct recruiting
functions until an approved appeal, rebuttal, or adjudication is received from the appropriate
authority.

   b. Recruiting Standards Branch will:

  (1) Provide oversight on the completion of local and centralized screenings for all ARNG
personnel serving in or nominated for recruiting and training cadre positions. Oversight includes
auditing systems of record including but not limited to IPPS-A and/or current recruiting
management systems for compliance and transparency.

  (2) Process Type II offense appeal and/or rebuttal requests to authority for disposition.

  (3) Provide a quarterly consolidated report of approvals, disapprovals, removals, and
approved or disapproved appeal packets to the Office of the Army DCS, G1 Suitability Division.

  (4) Provide suitability training and roster reviews as requested or required. Conduct and
schedule training with new points of contact within 90 days of receipt of RSB Form 2A. Conduct

  7

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements

all other training and roster reviews based on current compliance rates (>95%/Green; 94.9-
90%/Amber; <90%/Red; Goal: 100%). At a minimum, a suitability status review will be
conducted annually with each RRB. States, Territories, Districts are excepted if they are already
scheduled for a Staff Assistance Visit for the current FY. Out-of-cycle or refresher training can
be requested via the RSB Suitability group email.

10. All HRR/RSB Forms pertaining to suitability screening and appeals are available on the
Recruiting Standards Branch (RSB SharePoint) SharePoint at https://armyeitaas.sharepoint-
mil.us/sites/ARNG-G1-HRr.

11. This message remains valid until rescinded by this office.

12. Point of contact for this memorandum is the Recruiting Standards Branch at ng.ncr.ngb-
arng.mbx.hrr-suitability@army.mil.

Program

ARNG-ARNG-HRR (600-37a)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-028, Suitability Screening and Compliance Requirements
Appendix B, Offense by Type (AR 600-78, Chapter 3-5)
  Offenses that result in a civilian or military criminal conviction or a finding of guilty in a field grade Article 15,
  UCMJ proceedings are automatic disqualifiers for appointment to, or retention in, a designated position.
  These offenses have no expiration, and the disqualification may not be appealed.
  Possessing, receiving, or viewing child pornography (Article 134 UCMJ).
  Rape or sexual assault (Article 120 or 134 UCMJ).
  Any offense punishable under UCMJ Articles 80, 120, 120b, 128, 134, and 130; similar civilian offenses
 Type I
  (rape, sexual assault, aggravated sexual contact, abusive sexual contact, stalking, sexual abuse of a child);
  or any attempt to commit such acts (Article 80, UCMJ).
  Inappropriate relationships and prohibited activities between recruits and recruiters and between trainers
  providing entry-level training and trainees (DoDI 1304.33 Enclosure 3, 1a(1) (a-c)/Article 93a).
  Domestic violence or child abuse as described by DoDI 6400.06 (Article 128 UCMJ), child abuse, or any
  violent crime under the UCMJ.
  Previous separation from any Service for any Type I offense listed above.
  A requirement to be registered as a sex offender.
  Offenses meeting the definition of adverse information will also result in automatic disqualification for
  appointment to, or retention in, a designated position and are limited to those that occurred during the
  Soldier’s military career (including Sister Services). A Type II offense may be appealed. All appeals are
  final.
  Sexual harassment to include influencing, threatening a person’s career, pay or job (Article 93 or 132).
  Prostitution or pandering (Article 134).
  Fraternization (Article 134).
 Type II  Participation in extremist organizations and activities by Army personnel inconsistent with the
  responsibilities of military service (as defined in AR 600–20).
  Special, general court-martial conviction that results in any civilian criminal felony convictions.
  Criminal offense involving a child.
  Extramarital sexual conduct or inappropriate relationship (Article 134).
  Wrongful broadcast or distribution of intimate visual images (Article 117a UCMJ).
  Wrongful use possession, distribution, importation, or exportation of a controlled substance (Article 112a
  UCMJ).
  Initial enlistment waivers for derogatory information related to any Type I offense.
  Type I offenses for which a Soldier was not convicted in a court of law or did not receive an Article 15 or
  higher UCMJ action (Includes DoDI 1304.33, Enclosure 3, 1a(1)(a-c))
  Alcohol abuse (as defined in 5 CFR 731.202(b)(5)).
  Offenses meeting the definition of adverse information and committed within 5 years of the date of a
  Soldier’s nomination, may be disqualifying for appointment to, or retention in, a designated position. An
  approval authority may favorably adjudicate a Type III offense. A Type III offense may be appealed. All
  appeals are final.
  Relief for cause noncommissioned officer evaluation report or officer evaluation reports in current grade.
 Type III   Previous separation from any service for any Type III offense.
  Initial enlistment waivers for derogatory information (not related to an offense listed in Type II).
  Assault (other than categories listed in Type I).
  Larceny, fraud, or robbery (Articles 121, 124, or 122, UCMJ).
  Burglary (Article 129).
  Prohibited activities related to recruiting efforts, future Soldiers, or initial entry trainees that fall under DoDI

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-022, Prior Service Basic Combat Training (BCT) Update

chunks.title: SMOM 25-017: Live Scan Procedures
chunks.text:
NATIONAL GUARD BUREAU
  111 SOUTH GEORGE MASON DRIVE
  ARLINGTON VA 22204-1373

ARNG-HRR-O (RN 600)  30 April 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention Force

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-017, Updated Live Scan Procedures

1. References.

   a. Army Regulation 601-210 (Regular Army and Reserve Components Enlistment
Program)

   b. PPOM 24-017 (Accession Options Criteria (AOC)), 01 July 2024

   c. USMEPCOM Regulation 601-23 (Enlistment Processing), 26 February 2024

2. Purpose. Provide updated guidance on Live Scan (LS) or finger printing applicants
accessing. These changes allow for greater flexibility at the user level. Recruiting
personnel will be able to submit requests for exceptions in certain cases. These
procedures do not change the requirements set forth by AR 601-210 or USMEPCOM
Regulation 601-23.

3. All States, Puerto Rico, The Virgin Islands, Guam, and the District of Columbia will
submit fingerprints (FPs) electronically via LS devices utilizing Cross Match ArcID
https://livescanrsn.usarec.army.mil/#. Fingerprint submissions are required for all
applicants, to include Prior Service Field Enlistments, Non-MEPS Enlistments, and Direct
Commissioning and Accessions.

4. The following guidance is changed in the AOC Appendix J.

  a. Fingerprint results are not required for ASVAB testing and MEPS physical.
Applicants that were not Live Scan fingerprinted and are projected to “Physical Only,” an
“X” projection, must have MEPS fingerprints submitted prior to leaving the MEPS.
Applicants that intend to enlist must be projected to enlist, an “A” projection, may enlist if
fingerprint results are complete. Exceptions listed in 4d.

  b. Applicants are authorized to non-MEPS enlist (IAW local MEPS GC SOP) once
fingerprint results are posted in RZ and the enlistment “A” projection is reviewed and given
a “Go Packet” in process checkpoint. Non-MEPS applicants must have fingerprint results
that are not older than 100 days from the closed date on the Case Closing Transmittal.

ARNG-HRR-O (RN 600)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-017, Updated Live Scan Procedures

  c. The HRR Form 369 must be completed when the initial appointment is conducted.
The recruiter should ask the applicant questions, mark the applicable response, and sign
digitally. Only the recruiter should sign the form, while the applicant does not initial or sign
it. Ink or a wet signature is not authorized.

   d. Applicants may continue to process without Live Scan results for the reasons
below. Exceptions will be considered by the Accessions Suitability Office via suitability
workflow. Applicants that were granted an exception to enlist without fingerprint results will
be discharged if an undisclosed 300 level or higher law violation returns on a Rap Sheet,
regardless of disposition. Retain is not authorized.

   Exceptions include:

  (1) Sustained Equipment failure

  (2) Sustained Network issues

  (3) Inclement weather

  (4) Safety concerns

  (5) Excessive travel distance

  e. To request an exception or for support contact the ASO at (502) 684-3241 or (502)
684-3245 or for general questions email to usarmy.knox.ngb.mbx.arng-accessions-
suitability@army.mil or the MS Teams message to ASO with an attached screen shot.

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention Force

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-015, REAL-ID Implementation

1. Reference. USAREC Message 25-023, dated 04 March 2025.

2. Purpose. Beginning on 7 May 2025 all ARNG personnel, applicants, and shippers entering a
Military Entrance Processing facility will be required to possess a REAL-ID or an approved alternate
form of identification to be granted access. Additionally, all Warriors are required to have a REAL-ID or

a form of identification for purposes like accessing government facilities and boarding flights. More
information can be found on the DHS website.

4. Commands will confirm that all Recruiters, RSP cadre, and Recruiting and Retention personnel as
well as applicants, and shippers possess a REAL-ID or an approved alternate form of identification
before making any movement on or after 7 May 2025.

   b.   U.S. Dept. of Defense ID

chunks.text:

ARNG-HRR (RN 601-210)  10 April 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention Force

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-013 Changes to Processing English as a Second Language
Applicants

1. References.

  a. AR 601-210, Regular Army and Reserve Components Enlistment Program.

  b. ARNG PPOM 24-017 (Accession Options Criteria), dated 01 July 2024.

  c. U.S. MEPCOM Regulation (UMR) 611-1 dated 18 March 2024.

2. This message provides clarification and new requirements for ARNG applicants who
may speak English as their second language.

3. The ARNG has seen an increase in the number of Warriors entering military service
who do not speak and comprehend English. Recruiting personnel must ensure that all
applicants who speak English as a second language and still have difficulty reading,
writing, and comprehending English are appropriately identified and take the English
Comprehension Language Test (ECLT). Trainees that arrive at reception and are
determined not to meet language standards will be REFRAD to their state.

4. All Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs) who have been in the United States for less
than three (3) years at the time of processing for enlistment must be projected to take the
ECLT.

5. Acceptable documents for validating time in country.

   a. United States Customs and Immigration Services, Form I-551

   b. Foreign Visa

   c. Education Transcript

ARNG-HRR (RN 601-210)
SUBJECT: SMOM 25-013, Changes to Processing English as a Second Language
Applicants

6. CAT-IV or 09M Applicant requirements.

  a. Every applicant holding a USCIS Form I-551 (Permanent Resident Card) and
entering as a potential CAT-IV or 09M program (AFQT 16-30), regardless of length of time
in the United States, is required to complete the ECLT before contracting.

7. No exception to policy is authorized for applicants who do not meet the 3-year
requirement. Recruiters must ensure that the applicant’s primary and secondary
languages are annotated in the Foreign Language section of Recruiter Zone. Enclosure,
Memo Exempt Countries, provides a list of countries excused from the ECLT. Follow
guidance from paragraph 3, if there is any indication that the applicant is not meeting the
language requirements.

8. An ECLT score remains in an applicant’s permanent record. The score cannot be
removed, regardless of whether it is determined that the applicant may not have needed to
take it initially. The applicant can retest IAW, UMR 611-1.

9. The POCs for this message is MSG Janelle Taua-Freitas, ROC NCOIC at
janelle.a.taua-freitas.mil@army.mil or (509) 385-1391 or Mr. Matt Saracco, MEPS
Program Manager at matthew.r.saracco.civ@army.mil or (717) 798-5199.

chunks.title: SMOM 25-006: Urgent Medical Waiver Processing
chunks.text:
NATIONAL GUARD BUREAU
  111 SOUTH GEORGE MASON DRIVE
  ARLINGTON VA 22204-1373

ARNG-HRR-O  6 JANUARY 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention Force

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-006 - Urgent Medical Waiver Requests “Same-Day” Processing

Guidance
1. Reference. PPOM 24-017 Accessions Option Criteria, dated 16 July 2024.

2. Purpose: To inform the Recruiting and Retention force on changes to the urgent waiver requests
processing timeline. Effective 6 Jan. 2025 urgent medical waiver requests “Same-Day” will be
accepted in the following circumstances:

   a. Applicants at reception battalion.
   b. Applicants with the following medical disqualifications: hearing loss, eye disqualifications,
allergies (except peanuts and stinging insects), and simple orthopedic DQs with a documented
focused exam. Multiple disqualifications will not be considered for an urgent waiver.

3. All urgent or “Same-Day” requests must be loaded in MATS then followed by an email
submitted to ROB waivers at ng.ncr.ngb-arng.list.hrr-rob-waivers-mil@army.mil. All email
submissions must include the applicant’s state, full name, and last 4 of the social security
number. Requests will not be accepted through any communication other than email.

4. In most cases, urgent waivers will be processed within 1-hour of delivery of the request.
Requests will be accepted until 1800 EST; anything received after that time will be processed
the following business day. There may be certain days or periods during a day that a 1-hour
response is not feasible. We will notify individuals or States when we cannot handle the current
workload. However, we will apply a 1-hour standard in all accepted urgent waiver cases.

5. Urgent waiver requests for medical disqualifications that do not meet the criteria in 3.b. will be
reviewed in the order received as a regular medical waiver request. Requesters will be notified
by email if the urgent waiver does not meet the “Same-Day” qualifications.

6. The point of contact for this message is LTC Stefanie Carone at stefanie.a.carone.mil@army.mil
or (401) 954-3788.

  TIMOTHY R. SMITH
  COL, AG
  Chief, Strength Maintenance Division
  Army National Guard

MEMORANDUM FOR Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention (RRF)

SUBJECT: SMOM 25-003 - Processing 09M and CAT IV-A Applicants for Enlistment
in FY25

1. References.

  a. AR 601-210 (Regular Army and Reserve Components Enlistment Program)

  b. ARNG Personnel Policy Division, ARNG-HRH memorandum (FY25 Army National
Guard Accession Options Criteria, PPOM 24-017), 16 July 2024

  c. Department of Defense Instruction 1145.01, “Qualitative Distribution of Military
Manpower,” 12 December 2013, incorporating Change 2, 4 May 2020

2. Purpose: This SMOM provides the processing procedures and CAT IV-A allocations
for FY25. All 09M (T7) enlistments will be the primary vehicle for recruiting CAT IVs.
States, Territories and Districts are allocated a certain number of allowable CAT IV-A
because ARNG must adhere to the 4% CAT IV requirement outlined in the Qualitative
Distribution of Military Manpower Policy. Throughout the year, the CAT IV-A percentage
will encompass 09M enlistments, 16-20/Tier 2 CAT IV-A’s, and FLRI (09C) enlistments.

   a. Program Utilization. The ARNG offers three enlistment options for CAT IV-A
applicants based on aptitude and qualifications outlined in paragraph 1c of this
document. RRBs are charged with the responsibility to appropriately use, manage, and
track all CAT IV-A accessions.

  (1) Traditional CAT IV-A (AFQT 16-20): Applicants who are otherwise qualified
with valid line scores will count against a State, Territory, or Districts CAT IV-A
percentage for the duration of FY25.

  (2) Future Soldier Preparatory Course/09M CAT IV-A (AFQT 21-30): Applicants
who are otherwise qualified to participate in the 09M program will count against a State,
Territory, or Districts CAT IV-A percentage for the duration of FY25 unless the Warrior
retests and qualifies as a CAT III-B or higher upon the completion of the program.

  (3) Foreign Language Recruiting Initiative (FLRI)/09C CAT IV-A (AFQT 21-30):
Applicants who are otherwise qualified to participate in the 09C program will count

against a State, Territory, or Districts CAT IV-A percentage for the duration of FY25
unless the Warrior retest and qualifies as a CAT III-B or higher upon completion of the

  (2) Traditional CAT IVs were allocated by States, Territories and Districts based
on the FY25 mission letter. States should exhaust all allocations within the assigned
quarter (see enclosure). The ROC will not authorize allocations to be rolled over to the
following quarter.

  (3) CAT IVs will be restricted in the 4th quarter to ensure the overall CAT IV % is
under the threshold and we can fill FY26 09M seats.

  b. Enlistment Criteria:

  (1) 16-20 AFQT or 16-30 AFQT and Tier II education.

  (2) Must have at least two documented ASVAB scores to include recently expired
tests.

  (3) Current Physical and DAT results required (approved medical waiver if

  (4) Meet initial entry body fat requirements (ARMS and ARMS Expanded are not
authorized to enlist as a Traditional CAT IV).

  (5) Meet MOS line score requirements, eligible for Line Score Waiver, or

 1. DOMESTIC VIOLENCEOFFENSE(S):
  a. Domestic battery/violence offenses include, but are not limited to: Charge(s) of assault, simple assault, assault and battery, battery, assault with the
 intent to commit bodily harm, assault on a person, abuse, domestic violence or any offense that involves the use or attempted use of physical force, or
 threatened use of a deadly weapon by an applicant against their parent, stepparent, sister, or brother, spouse, child; by a person with whom the victim shares
 a child in common; by a person who is cohabiting with or has cohabited with the victim as a spouse, parent, or guardian; or by a person who was similarly
 situated to a spouse, parent, or guardian of the victim. Persons who are similarly situated to a spouse include two persons who are residing at the same
 location in an intimate relationship with the intent to make that place their home regardless of disposition.
  b. Enlistment of applicants with a qualifying conviction for domestic violence under the Lautenberg Amendment is prohibited. No waivers authorized (AR
 601-210 Para 4-7 and Table 4-4, Offense Code 414).

 2. DUI OFFENSE(S):
   a. A DUI waiver is required for any applicant who received an underage drinking and driving, wet and reckless, zero tolerance, and/or refusal to take
 breathalyzer or similar offenses.
   b. No waiver authorized for applicants with three or more separate DUI offenses.

 3. DRUG RELATEDOFFENSE(S):
  a. Applicants who incur charges of possession of marijuana and paraphernalia from the same incident who have no other charges may enlist without a
 waiver.
  b. Applicants who incur conviction or an OAD for sale/distribution of marijuana or any other controlled substance is non-waivable.
  c. NPS applicants with a positive DAT at MEPS require an approved suitability review from ASO after negative DAT results have posted in the record.

chunks.title: FY26 ARNG AOC (PPOM 25-042) - Ch 1-4: Eligibility & Waivers
chunks.text:
Chapter 1 - Introduction

1-1. Purpose
This policy prescribes eligibility criteria governing all accessions into the Army National
Guard (ARNG), processing procedures for enlisted, warrant officer, and officer
accessions using specific enlistment options. This policy is used in conjunction with AR
601-210 and is formatted so the chapters coincide with those in AR 601-210 (except
chapters 4, 5, 8, and 9). See AR 601-210 for chapters or paragraphs not listed in this
policy.

1-2. References
See Appendix A.

1-3. Explanation of abbreviations and terms
See Appendix L.

1-4. Authorized Signatures
  a. All enlistment documents that required either an initial/signature from the
applicant, RRNCO, and/or other military personnel must be signed/initialed by each
individually. Initials/signatures cannot be copied or duplicated; each initial/signature
must be unique.
  b. The use of Adobe to sign/initial a document by typing the RRNCO’s/applicant's
name (rendering a cursive font of the RRNCO’s/applicant’s name/initials) is not
authorized. Any document bearing a signature that is not unique (i.e., copy and pasted)
will be considered a falsified official document, RRNCO misconduct, a violation of
individual state’s Code of Conduct (Title 32) and Article 105 UCMJ – Forgery (Title 10)
as will any type of altering/editing of a previously signed form.
  c. Wet signatures are not authorized for any system generated forms pertaining to
the applicant’s enlistment contract. These forms include the DD Form 4, annexes or
addendums, and DD Form 1966 (page 3).

Chapter 2 - Enlistment in the Army National Guard for Non-Prior Service
applicants

2-1. General
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 25-015)
  a. Source documents. Source documents will be verified by the Section Chief
during the NCOIC QC Checkpoint. The only document required to be hand carried to
MEPS is a valid ID. ARNG personnel, applicants, and shippers entering a Military
Entrance Processing facility will be required to possess a REAL-ID or an approved
alternate form of identification to be granted access. Additionally, all Warriors are
required to have a REAL-ID or an approved alternate form of identification before
shipping to their initial training. A REAL-ID is a driver’s license or identification card that
is compliant with federal standards and is a form of identification for purposes like

2-2. Basic eligibility criteria for all Non-Prior Service Applicants
  a. All Non-Prior Service (NPS) and Glossary Non-Prior Service (GNPS) applicants
enlisting into the ARNG are required to be in a deployable status within 24 months of
enlistment. Federal law prohibits delays beyond 24 months.
  (1) Further guidance on 24-month IET requirements and waiver processing are
covered in AD 2025-04 and PPOM 25-023.
  (2) Officer Candidates must meet the requirements in Chapter 9.
  b. Religious accommodation (RA) requests will be processed IAW current ARNG
personnel policy. Applicants must be informed of the policy surrounding their specific
request and may begin processing their request prior to signing any accession
documentation. The applicant may wait for the decision prior to accessing to ensure
approval and exercise of their RA during IADT; however, if they wish to begin service
pending approval of their request, they will adhere to existing standards while waiting on
decision. Pre-accession requests must be processed within 30-days from initiation;
requests are not required to include all levels of intermediate Commanders allowing for
an expedited process.

2-4. Citizenship
  a. Applicants born outside of the United States or Territories must show proof of US
citizenship at the time of enlistment. The following documents are authorized as proof:
  (1) US Passport (can be expired if it was issued for 5 years or more), no
suitability review (SR) required. A US passport issued for less than 5 years may be
used if an ETP is approved by HQDA G-1. A Suitability Review (SR) is required.

least an active petition at USCIS to be eligible to ship to training. The State must
provide proof of an active petition.
  (2) 2-year conditional I-551 card holders will be allowed to enlist and ship if the I-

holders.

passport, or Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) form I-94. These are proof of 1 year
temporary I-551 status. All three require an SR approval to enlist. Approval will be
granted if the Applicant can enlist and ship with 6 months (180 days) or more time
remaining between the ship date and expiration date. The stamp or form must have the
statement “Upon endorsement serves as temporary I-551 evidencing permanent
residence for 1 year.”

certifying their adoption and a US State or Territory issued birth certificate registering
their birth abroad. Applicants without these documents are not authorized to enlist until
they have full citizenship documentation. These applicants are not authorized to use a
parent’s Naturalization information as their own. Recruiters should contact the ASO if
necessary for these cases.

2-8. Trainability
  a. NPS/GNPS applicants are eligible for enlistment provided they meet the
minimum criteria for enlistment as well as MOS specific test requirements.
  b. Aptitude overrides. These exceptions are processed by MEPS GC to ARNG-
HRR-ROC.
  (1) Telephonic or electronic overrides up to 5 points for select MOSs are
authorized. Points are not authorized to be split between multiple categories.
  (2) Aptitude overrides are not authorized in the General Technical (GT) Skilled
Technical (ST), or Electronics (EL) areas.
  (3) The ROC is not authorized to provide aptitude area overrides for MOS 27D or
89D or for CMFs 14, 15, 18, 25, 31, 35 or 68 (except 68G).
  c. Proponent ETP. These exceptions are processed through ARNG-HRR-O-ASO.
  (1) Exceptions for MOS qualifications will be considered by proponent as outlined
in DA Pam 611-21. Only the CMF proponent can grant exceptions to DA Pam 611-21
via workflow from the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO.
  (2) All proponent exceptions require a valid ASVAB score.
  (3) Once the MEPS GC contacts the ASO via workflow, the record will be locked
until proponent returns a response to the ETP. Proponents are not required to process
same day exceptions.
  d. All 15C, 15Q, and 15W Warriors must be shipped to Fort Jackson for BCT for
flight physicals. Applicants who do not pass the flight physical will be reclassified into
another MOS. MEPS GCs will ensure the DD Form 1966 is properly annotated in
"Remarks Review" with three alternate MOSs. ETPs to 15 series quals require a DA
4187.
  e. All 12M Warriors must be shipped to Fort Leonard Wood for BCT.
  f. Drug and alcohol abuse as it applies to MOS qualification questions will be
answered by proponent through the ASO.
  g. Additional Security Screening Requirements. See Appendix C.
  h. Applicants must have a ship date prior to the expiration of their physical.

2-9. Physical
There are three different Depth Perception tests that have been used for enlistment: the
Armed Services Vision Test (AFVT), the Multiple Circle Stereopsis Test (MCST), and
the Titmus test. The AFVT test is obsolete and will no longer be used for enlistment in
the ARNG. Any applicant receiving this test must be retested on either the MCST or
Titmus tests. The MCST test is being phased out in preference for the Titmus test.
Currently, either the MCST or Titmus test may be used for enlistment, without a waiver
or ETP requirement. At a future date to be announced, the MCST test will no longer be
acceptable. MOS 35G is the only MOS requiring a depth perception test. MOS 12Y no
longer requires a depth perception test for enlistment.
  a. Applicants with a temporary reservation for MOS 35G will be scheduled for
MCST or Titmus depth perception testing when the initial physical is scheduled. Each
MEPS will administer the MCST or Titmus upon request. MEPS GCs are responsible
for ensuring the test has been completed and passed. Reservations for MOS 35G will
not be made without a passing depth perception test score posted in MIRS. All other
testing will occur on the day of reservation processing provided MEPS medical
personnel are still present.
  b. RRNCOs or MEPS GCs will project the applicant for medical processing and
annotate the following in remarks: "Depth Perception test required for MOS 35G”.
  (1) Qualifying MCST score for MOS 35G:
  (a) Letter A-D signifies the test version or ‘plate’ used.
  (b) PASS: Number scores 7-12.
  (c) FAIL: Number score 6 or below.
  (d) Waiver/ETP is not authorized for 6 or below.
  (2) Titmus scores for MOS 35G:
  (a) PASS: First number score of 6-9. Second number (Arc Seconds) must be
40 or lower.
  (b) FAIL: First number score of 1-5. Second number score of 50 or higher.
  (c) Waiver/ETP is not authorized for 50 Arc Seconds or higher.
  (3) To ensure each applicant possesses qualifying scores the MEPS GC must
review the MEPS Medical Exam Note prior to pulling a reservation or converting a
temporary reservation to a permanent reservation. Must contact the ROC to verify
passing MCST/Titmus (via uploaded screen shot of MIRS Vision "test scores" to ERM)
and placement of depth perception override in Web REQUEST (prior to pulling training).
  c. The MHS Genesis Medical Exam Note will not be uploaded into RZ. The Medical
Exam note should only be uploaded into MATS for medical review purposes.

2-11. Conduct and administrative criteria
  a. If a city or county does not have their own police agency and/or is covered by
another agency, and/or arrest records are maintained by another agency, the RRNCO
will annotate accordingly in block 12 of DD Form 369 explaining which agency has
jurisdiction over that area. The RRNCO will complete blocks 14-16 and enter the city
name in the agency block.
  b. If law enforcement agencies will not complete DD Form 369, but will allow
recruiting personnel to view the records, the RRNCO will complete and sign the DD
Form 369. In so doing, the RRNCO will include a comment stating they have viewed
the police records that relate to the alleged offense or offenses. RRNCOs will complete
the DD Form 369 blocks 14-16, state in block 13 name and number of the agency
contacted and complete the Law Enforcement Agency block.
  c. If city and/or county police agencies claim they report all arrests and citations to
their State website, they must state so in writing in the same manner as AR 601-210
para 2-11e. The use of USAREC Police Agency List (PAL) is not authorized.
  d. The use of the DD Form 369 is restricted to police/sheriff/trooper only; they are
not to be used for court record checks. State websites are only authorized for State
required DD Form 369 Police Record Checks as outlined in AR 601-210 para 2-11a. If
city and/or county police agencies claim they report all arrests and citations to their
State website, they must state so in writing per AR 601-210 para 2-11e.
  e. Applicants with disqualifications:
  (1) Applicants who claim the following conduct offenses require the police agency
report, court document, or other records to clearly identify the other person involved:
  (a) Assault, simple assault, fighting, or battery.
  (b) Domestic battery and/or violence.
  (c) Unauthorized use of a vehicle or joyriding.
  (2) Applicants who claim the following offenses require the police agency report,
court document, or other records with the dollar value to determine the offense level:
  (a) Check, worthless, making or uttering, with intent to defraud or deceive.
  (b) Illegal and/or fraudulent use of a credit card, bankcard, or automated card.
  (c) Grand larceny, larceny, or conversion.
  (d) Stolen property knowingly received.
  (3) Applicants who claim the following conduct offenses require a police agency
report or other records to determine the nature of the offense:
  (a) Indecent exposure.
  (b) Contributing to delinquency of minor.
  (c) Any offense that originated as a charge that was sexual in nature.
  (4) Applicants who receive additional punishment (additional fine, suspended
license, extended probation, etc.) for failure to appear, failure to pay fine, or contempt of
court is considered an Other Adverse Disposition (OAD). Questionable cases are to be
sent to ARNG-HRR-O-ASO for SR.

2-16. Authorized enlistment periods
   a. NPS/GNPS applicants will be enlisted for 8 years. Active participation in an
ARNG or USAR unit is service in the Selected Reserve (SELRES). An applicant may
choose one of the following options:
  (1) 8 x 0 (8 years SELRES). This option requires the Soldier to remain an active
participant in an ARNG unit for 8 years.
  (2) 6 x 2 (6 years SELRES). This option requires the Soldier to remain an active
participant in an ARNG unit for 6 years with 2 years remaining Military Service
Obligation (MSO).
  (3) 4 x 4 (4 years SELRES). This option requires the Soldier to remain an active
participant in an ARNG unit for 4 years with 4 years remaining MSO.
  (4) 3 x 5 (3 years SELRES). This option requires the Soldier to remain an active
participant in an ARNG unit for 3 years with 5 years remaining MSO.
   b. Applicants enlisting into a training path requiring 34 or more weeks of Initial Entry
Training (IET) must enlist for a minimum of 6 x 2 contractual obligation.

Chapter 4 - Enlistment waiver and suitability processing

Section I General

4-1. Purpose
The ARNG will adhere to waiver requirements as outlined in AR 601-210 and this policy
as it pertains to conduct in need of a waiver, administrative, or medical disqualifications,
except in cases where the ARNG imposes a more constraining requirement. Additional
factors to consider are time since the offense, additional charges, AFQT score,
education level, volunteer work, professional and character references, and steady
employment; also referred to as the “whole-person-concept”.
  a. Conduct waiver and suitability processing procedures are aimed at identifying
and screening applicants who could present disciplinary problems. Misconduct
offenses pose serious questions to an applicant’s fitness for service, as do an excessive
number of minor traffic or non-traffic offenses. Such applicants are likely to become
serious disciplinary problems and could divert resources from the performance of
military missions. Commanders are charged with the responsibility of recommending
waivers for applicants who satisfy the concerns of the receiving commander, have been
rehabilitated, are acceptable candidates from a conduct standpoint and who possess a
documented meritorious waiver request.
  b. Administrative waivers are considered on a case-by-case basis for applicants
who have shown growth and significant potential for productive service, and who are
otherwise qualified.
  c. Medical waivers are reviewed when a condition is considered disqualifying under
standards established by DoDI 6130.03, Vol 1. The objective is to procure and retain
personnel who may be capable of serving despite their medically disqualifying condition.

4-2. Responsibilities
   a. The Director of Army National Guard (DARNG) is the approval authority for
ARNG waivers.
   b. ARNG-HRR is responsible for processing waivers for meritorious individuals
concerning disqualifications outlined in AR 601-210. Questions pertaining to waivers

4-6. Medical Waiver Timelines
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 25-006)
Medical waivers will be processed in the order they are received. Medical waivers are
processed as quickly as possible based on workload and staffing.
  a. Urgent (or “same-day”) medical waiver requests will be accepted for the
following:
  (1) Applicants at reception battalion.
  (2) Applicants with the following medical disqualifications: hearing loss, eye
disqualifications, allergies (except peanuts and stinging insects), and simple orthopedic
DQs with a documented focused exam. Multiple disqualifications will not be considered
for an urgent waiver.
  b. All same day requests must be loaded into MATS and then followed by an email
submitted to ROB waivers at ng.ncr.ngb-arng.list.hrr-rob-waivers-mil@army.mil. All
email submissions must include the applicant’s state and full name. Requests will not
be accepted through any communication other than email.
  c. In most cases, same day waivers will be processed within 1 hour of receipt.
Requests will be accepted until 1800 EST; anything received after that time will be
processed the following business day. There may be certain days or periods during a
day when a 1-hour response is not feasible; individuals or States will be notified when
there is a high workload. However, a 1-hour standard will be applied in all accepted
urgent waiver cases.
  d. Same-day waiver requests for medical disqualifications that do not meet the
criteria in 3b will be reviewed in the order received as a regular medical waiver request.
Requesters will be notified by email if the urgent waiver does not meet the same-day
qualifications.

4-12. Exception for tattoos and brandings
  a. All applicants will complete an NGB Form 902 that properly annotates each
tattoo, tattoo location on applicant’s body, and if they are compliant IAW AR 670-1, para

outlined in AR 670-1 para 3-3, the RRC will make the initial determination regarding
tattoo compliance. Applicants who claim to have no tattoos will complete the NGB Form
902, annotate appropriately, and the RRNCO will sign. The NGB Form 902 will be
loaded in the applicant’s record under tattoo screening form.
  b. Applicants who have tattoos on the head and face (except permanent makeup),
violate the Army’s tattoo policy regarding location, to include inside the eyelids, mouth,
and ears.
  c. Army policy governing tattoos authorizes applicants to have:
  (1) One visible tattoo on each hand (including the palm), not to exceed one inch
in measurement in all directions; an unlimited number of tattoos between the fingers if
they are not visible when the fingers are closed; and one ring tattoo on each hand.
  (2) One tattoo on the back on the neck, not to exceed two inches in measurement
in all directions.
  (3) One tattoo behind each ear, not to exceed one inch in measurement in all
directions, not to extend forward of the ear lobe.
  d. TAG is the only approval authority for final determinations. Memorandums with
alternate signatures, even if signature authority has been delegated, are not authorized.

4-15. Positive drug or alcohol tests (BAT/DAT)
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 24-020)
  a. Any applicant who was or is confirmed positive for the presence of drugs or
alcohol at time of original physical examination is not eligible for enlistment/shipping.
  b. PS and GNPS applicants who test positive for the presence of drugs or alcohol at
MEPS will not be considered for a waiver. Applicants who accessed into an RC and
subsequently discharged because of positive DAT results prior to shipping to training
are eligible for DAT waiver consideration.
  c. If an applicant’s first test is positive for THC, they must wait 90 days from the
receipt of positive results before returning to MEPS for retest.
  (1) If an applicant’s second test is negative, a TAG level DAT waiver may be
requested.
  (2) If the applicant’s second test is positive, the applicant is permanently
disqualified and no waivers or exceptions to policy will be considered.
  d. If applicant’s first test is positive for any drug other than marijuana (including
synthetics) they must wait 1-year from the receipt of the positive results before returning
to MEPS for a retest.
  (1) If applicant’s second test is negative, an NGB Level DAT waiver may be
requested.
  (2) If applicant’s second test is positive, the applicant is permanently disqualified
and no waivers or exceptions to policy will be considered.
  e. Enlistees who are confirmed positive for the presence of any drugs or alcohol at
time of physical examination at MEPS will be processed for separation as outlined in AR
135-178.
  f. All applicants who test positive will be required to have police record checks
accomplished as part of the waiver process regardless of any admission or record of
civil offenses. Police record checks and live scan results are required for all DAT
waivers, checks will be obtained as stated in AR 601-210, and new police record checks
are required to be obtained as stated in AR 601-210.

4-16. Counseling of applicants
To prevent frustration and confusion on the part of both the RRNCO and the applicant,
care should be taken in counseling applicants on waivers.
RRNCO(s) will explain to applicants that their application for waiver of disqualification
was not favorably considered. However, under no circumstances will the RRNCO
disclose the name or organization of the final disposition authority, nor will any recruiting
personnel contact the final disposition authority. Waiver inquiries will be submitted
through ARNG-HRR-O. In processing PS waivers, the individual should be advised that
the denial of the waiver was after a thorough evaluation of their PS records in
conjunction with their current waiver request. Only those documents which belong to
the applicant will be returned. Waiver memorandums or copies will not be returned to
the applicant. The correspondence pertaining to the determination of waivers will be
filed and maintained at TAG level only.

4-17. Extremist affiliation
Use the procedures below to determine eligibility when suspected affiliation is reported,
by visual sighting or annotation on any enlistment document, through tattoos, behavior,
verbal or written communication, appearance, or gestures that an individual is or may
be involved with an extremist organization, group, or gang. Enlistment documents
include, but are not limited to, police reports, court documents, or school incidents.
  a. The RRC must ensure from a series of direct and indirect questions the applicant
is given a fair assessment and determination without personal bias or a predetermined
outcome.
  b. A person who admits to or is determined to have been associated with, or a
member of a gang linked to criminal activity, or an extremist group or organization will
be interviewed concerning their involvement. When interviewing applicants, the whole
person concept will be applied. Criminal background, commander interview, and a
potential for meeting Army standards must be reviewed and considered.
  c. Applicants who are in fact members of any extremist organization or member of a
gang associated with criminal activity do not meet the standard for enlistment. No
waiver authorized.
  (1) Extremist or Affiliation SR: When submitting SR, an RRC memorandum and
recommendation must include details that address when the extremist/hate/gang
affiliation took place, what organization the applicant was affiliated with, evidence or
proof they are no longer affiliated, and why they were affiliated.
  (2) Debarred SR: When submitting an SR a RRC memorandum and
recommendation must include details behind the applicant being debarred (when,
where, and why). When applicable, police and court record checks must be included in
these reviews.
  (3) Applicants requiring one of the above SR do not require an ASVAB or
physical prior to submission of the review.
  (4) Applicants identified as requiring a review will be prescreened with an ASVAB
pre-test, completed medical prescreen (DD Form 2807-2), and Live Scan results.
  (5) The HRR 369, once completed and uploaded, will serve as proof the applicant
has been screened for extremist affiliation.
  (6) Applicants with admitted charge(s) above traffic level offenses (level 100) will
have police/court checks that show the final disposition of the charge(s) prior to the
suitability workflow submission.
  d. Definitions.
  (1) Extremism. An individual that advocates for any of the following:
  (a) Hatred or bias based on race, sex, sexual orientation, or ethnicity.
  (b) Creating or engaging in discrimination based on race, color, sex, national
origin, religion, or sexual orientation.
  (c) Use of force or violence or unlawful means to deprive individuals of their
rights to pursue political or religious goals.
  (d) Support for terrorist or criminal organizations or objectives.
  (e) Overthrow of the US Government by force, violence, or sedition.
  (f) Subversion (i.e., violations of law, disobedience to lawful orders or
regulations).

4-18. Suitability
The ARNG will adhere to requirements for SR as outlined in AR 601-210 and all other
references pertaining to suitability. All GNPS and PS applicants require an SR.
Applicants who require an SR must have an approved SR workflow prior to any MEPS
processing.
  a. ARNG-HRR-O-ASO is the determining authority for ARNG suitability reviews, to
include the following:
  (1) Domestic violence/domestic crimes. Applicants who are charged with any
type of domestic violence/domestic crime (as defined in Table 4-1), regardless of final
disposition.
  (2) Sex crimes (any offense of a sexual nature). Applicants charged with any
type of sex crime, regardless of final disposition.
  (3) Adult/juvenile felony charge(s) under the local law and any offense(s) listed as
major misconduct, regardless of the final disposition.
  (4) Any charges listed in Table 4-3 where the ASO is listed as SR authority.
  (5) Having a weapon on school grounds.
  b. A SR will be QCd and processed via RZ workflow with a recommendation by the
State Waivers Analyst recommending approval.
  c. The required documentation for the submission of SR includes:
  (1) Applicant Statement.
  (2) NGB Form 905.
  (3) Any additional forms as required by State operations.
  d. The whole person concept will be applied in determining applicant qualifications.
  e. SR approval does not indicate the enlistment packet is complete.
  f. ARNG-HRR-O-ASO does not approve or disapprove waivers but will recommend
follow-on actions to be conducted to clarify any deficiencies.
